newsitem.title: GERMANY: Schering's Pohle sees 96 net profit 330-340 mln DM.
newsitem.headline: Schering's Pohle sees 96 net profit 330-340 mln DM.

text.p: Schering AG's chief financial officer Klaus Pohle said on Monday that the German drugs company made a net profit of 330 to 340 million marks in 1996, up more than 35 percent.
Pohle made his comments in response to an enquiry by Reuters.
In November, Schering said nine-month net profit rose to 286 million marks, up 66 percent, while sales rose 12 percent to 3.85 billion.
Pohle also said that sales growth should rise by at least a two digit figure.

Pohle said the record profit figure for 1996 was pressured by the acquisition of Jenapharm and Leiras. He said Leiras would only affect the last four months and Jenapharm the last three months of the balance sheet.

Schering made sales of 4.647 billion marks and profits of 249 million marks in 1995, when currency turmoil seriously dented profits. In an advanced publication of an interview with Tuesday's edition of the daily Berliner Zeitung, Shering chief executive Giuseppe Vita also said net profit would be 330-340 million marks for 1996 and sales would probably be more than the forecast 5.2 billion marks.
Vita expected a further dividend increase in 1997 and said Schering wanted to give shareholders a dividend of two marks for 1996 rather than 1.55 marks.
Vita also said an out-of-court settlement was possible in the dispute between Schering subsidiary Berlex and the U.S. firm Biogen over the patent rights for the multiple sclerosis drug Betaferon.
